title: བསྟན་འགྱུར། སྡེ་དགེ། དབུ་མ། ཁི (Derge Tengyur, vol. 111)
shelf_note: Derge Tengyur woodblock folio (margin volume letter ཁི), verse on bodhisattva conduct (purification of body and of resources/right livelihood); belongs in the Tengyur Madhyamaka volume.

ocr_errors.problem: suffix dropped on 'habituation'; both translations read it as habituation anyway

tr_errors_A.english: Speaking pleasantly and deceitfully for the purpose of gain and honor is flattery.
tr_errors_A.problem: གསོང་པོ means honest/straightforward (i.e. speaking in a seemingly upright, sweet way); rendered as its opposite 'deceitfully'

tr_errors_A.english: is anger and passion. Therefore, by abandoning attachment
tr_errors_A.problem: causal 'because anger follows on attachment' flattened into an identity statement; argument still recoverable

tr_errors_A.english: nor walking with ostentatiously measured steps

tr_errors_B.english: just as one openly treats others with respect
tr_errors_B.problem: བརྙས་ means contempt/disparagement; B turns it into 'respect', inverting the comparison in the self-other exchange verse

tr_errors_B.english: Speaking pleasantly but untruthfully for the sake of gain and honor is sycophancy.
do not cast their steps broadly or out of sequence
tr_errors_B.problem: 'out of sequence' is not in རིམ་གྱིས (gradually)

tr_errors_B.english: flattery or false gentleness, and never speaks in a diminished or subservient manner
tr_errors_B.problem: padded into three items; 'false' and 'subservient' added

pages.prefer_reason: B inverts བརྙས་ (contempt) into 'respect' in the opening verse, while A's errors are a shared moderate slip on གསོང་པོ and minor interpretive wording.

book_verdict: Transcription of this Derge folio is close to the print throughout; translation A is a faithful verse rendering, while B reverses one key word (contempt read as respect), which an expert reader would flag.
